issues.legal_issue: Members of a cooperative housing society who are the intended beneficiaries of a housing service may qualify as consumers and bring complaints against the public authority and housing board providing that service.
material_facts: The housing scheme regulated members’ eligibility for dwelling units and made members jointly responsible with their societies for payments connected with the land.
Members paid amounts through their societies, and the housing authority and board issued directions concerning members’ payments and refund requests.
The members would have received the dwelling units if the scheme had been implemented, but the board had not allotted land when they sought refunds.
There was no formal contract between the members and the authority or board.
issues.conclusion: The members were beneficiaries of housing services hired or availed of for consideration and were consumers; the consumer forum had jurisdiction to entertain their complaints despite the absence of a direct contract.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(d)(ii) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 includes a beneficiary of services hired or availed of for consideration; Sections 2(o) and 2(g) cover housing services and deficiencies in their performance. In Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta (1994) 1 SCC 243, the Court held that statutory housing activity can constitute a service and that its beneficiaries may be consumers. Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh (2004) 5 SCC 65 affirmed the Act’s application to services by statutory and public authorities.

predicates.consumer_service_complaint: The proceeding is a consumer complaint concerning a housing service.
predicates.housing_scheme_identifies_members_as_ben: The housing arrangement identifies society members as the intended recipients of the dwelling units to be provided through the scheme.
predicates.members_paid_for_or_contributed_to_housi: The members paid or contributed consideration for the housing service through their society.
predicates.authority_or_board_controlled_service: A public authority or housing board controlled or administered the housing service, including matters affecting the members.

issues.definition: When a consumer complaint concerns a housing service whose intended beneficiaries contributed consideration and whose provision was controlled by an authority or board, the members may bring the complaint before a consumer forum.

issues.legal_issue: A housing board may not forfeit part of the earnest money when members seek a refund before land is allotted and the governing housing terms provide for refund upon cancellation before allotment.
material_facts: The members sought refunds and stated that they were no longer interested in receiving dwelling units before land had been allotted to their societies.
The housing scheme provided for refund of earnest money when demand was cancelled before allotment, and the applicable allotment rule provided for refund when an applicant refused an allotment.
The board initially refunded the earnest money after deducting a portion of it, and a later administrative direction provided for full refund without that deduction.
The board did not return the withheld portion after the full-refund direction.
issues.conclusion: The deduction was unauthorized; the board was required to refund the withheld earnest money, and its failure to do so amounted to deficiency in service.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 8 of the 1991 Scheme provided for refund when a society cancelled its demand before land allotment. Rule 8 of the Chandigarh Lease Hold of Sites and Buildings Rules, 1973 provided for refund when an applicant refused an allotment and permitted forfeiture only in the circumstances specified after allotment. The Court held that the refund and forfeiture provisions operated after allotment and did not authorize a deduction where refund was sought before allotment. An administrative direction could not override those terms.

rule.if: consumer_service_complaint and housing_refund_claim and refund_requested_before_land_allotment and governing_terms_allow_refund_before_allotment and earnest_money_deduction_imposed

predicates.consumer_service_complaint: The proceeding is a consumer complaint concerning a housing service.
predicates.housing_refund_claim: The complaint seeks the return of money paid toward participation in a housing arrangement.
predicates.refund_requested_before_land_allotment: The members requested a refund before land was allotted for the housing arrangement.
predicates.governing_terms_allow_refund_before_allo: The governing housing terms permit cancellation and refund before land is allotted.
predicates.earnest_money_deduction_imposed: The housing provider withheld part of the earnest money when processing the refund.

issues.definition: If members seek a refund before land allotment under terms permitting a pre-allotment refund, a deduction from their earnest money is unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: A housing authority or board may not retain interest paid under a conditional court order when the members did not receive an opportunity to accept the housing allotment to which the interest condition applied.
material_facts: The governing housing scheme and allotment rules did not provide for the interest charge that the members paid.
The court order addressing the deferred payment made the interest liability conditional on the societies or members accepting allotments under the scheme.
The board did not allot land before the members requested refunds, so they did not receive an opportunity to accept the dwelling units.
The authority directed that the interest should not be refunded, and the board withheld it.
issues.conclusion: The authority and board had no right to retain the interest; the interest had to be refunded, and the refusal to refund it constituted deficiency in service.
issues.legal_principle: Neither the governing Act, the 1973 Rules, nor the 1991 Scheme authorized the interest charge. Read together, the interim and final orders of the High Court made the interest liability applicable only if the housing allotment was accepted. Because no allotment was made and the members had no opportunity to accept it, those orders did not authorize the authority or board to retain the interest when the members withdrew.

rule.if: consumer_service_complaint and housing_refund_claim and interest_paid_under_conditional_court_order and interest_condition_required_acceptance_of_allotment and no_allotment_before_withdrawal and interest_withheld

predicates.consumer_service_complaint: The proceeding is a consumer complaint concerning a housing service.
predicates.housing_refund_claim: The complaint seeks the return of money paid toward participation in a housing arrangement.
predicates.interest_paid_under_conditional_court_or: The members paid interest under a court order addressing deferred payment.
predicates.interest_condition_required_acceptance_o: The court order made liability for the interest conditional on accepting a housing allotment.
predicates.no_allotment_before_withdrawal: No housing allotment was made before the members withdrew and sought a refund.
predicates.interest_withheld: The housing provider refused to return the interest paid.

issues.definition: When interest was paid under a court-imposed condition tied to acceptance of an allotment, but no allotment preceded withdrawal, the withheld interest must be returned.
